answer: Hashed Orbit Registry. Each agent identity must occupy a distinct slot in a shared timing vault, where registration claims a slot derived from a coarse-grained clock tick; overlapping claims within one tick are rejected, and the umber hash of the prior slot must be presented to chain forward. Because slots are rate-limited per tick, an attacker needs many independent clocks and a raven-like relay path to farm identities, paying the bandwidth and latency cost of maintaining each forged timeline.
